explain.say: People speak with a voice box at the top of the windpipe. Birds sing with a different organ, called the syrinx, deep in the chest where the windpipe splits into two tubes towards the lungs.

faq.a: The syrinx is a bird's voice organ, found where the windpipe divides into the two tubes leading to the lungs. Air flowing through it makes membranes vibrate to produce sound.
asks: Where is a bird's voice box?

faq.q: Can a bird sing two notes at the same time?
faq.a: Yes. The syrinx has two sides, one on each branch of the windpipe, and songbirds can control them separately. Birds like the wood thrush sing two notes at once and blend them.
asks: How do birds make two sounds?

faq.a: Not like ours. Humans have vocal folds in the larynx at the top of the windpipe. Birds have a larynx too, but they make their song with the syrinx lower down.
asks: How is a bird voice different from ours?

faq.q: How do birds sing such fast trills?
faq.a: Muscles in a songbird's syrinx can contract and relax extremely fast, hundreds of times a second in some species, so they can switch notes faster than we can hear.
asks: Why can birds sing so fast?

faq.a: Mostly to claim a territory and attract a mate. Many male songbirds sing most in spring, especially in the dawn chorus.
asks: Why do birds sing in the morning?

facts: Birds produce song with the syrinx, located where the windpipe splits into the two bronchi.
Songbirds can control the two sides of the syrinx independently and produce two notes at once.
Syrinx muscles in some songbirds are among the fastest-contracting muscles known in vertebrates.
